name: Weird units
seoDesc: Weird units: work out weird units from the regular units and the weird units. A free conversion calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the regular units and the weird units and the Weird units calculator solves for weird units. That makes it useful for a recipe, a shopping list, a travel plan or a form that asks for a unit you do not use. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Weird units calculator work?
sections.html:
The Weird units calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports weird units in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the unit type); then you type in the regular units, the weird units (2), the weird units (3) and the weird units (4).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Weird units calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Weird units=regular units
Your height=(17 ÷ 10) × regular units ÷ customized for you...
Regular units=weird units
Normal energy unit=weird energy unit
That's...=(10, (1 ÷ 10) × sound volume)
That's...=temperature

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Length, opening in meters
  • Weird length units, opening in footsteps 👣
  • Length, opening in meters
  • Weird height units, opening in LEGO bricks
  • Length, opening in millimeters
  • Weird thickness units, opening in human hairs
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Weird weight units, opening in bees 🐝

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Weird units calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Reading a recipe written in units you do not use
  • Checking a product listing against the measurements you work with
  • Filling in a form that asks for imperial or metric values
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the regular units and the weird units — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Weird units calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns weird units, derived from the regular units and the weird units. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Weird units calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the regular units and the weird units, which is 15 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter regular units in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Regular units opens in meters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Weird units calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
